Maintenance Report — MNT-0015-001

Asset: WELL-0015 (SW-23 Well 015, T200, Southwest Block 23) Equipment: downhole pump Work started: 18 Dec 2022 08:00 · Finished: 28 Dec 2022 13:00 · Well stopped for this job: 245 hours Crew lead: Daniel Foster (U-302) · Crew: Brian Coleman · Contractor: Sandstone Rod & Pump Triggered by: inspection INS-0015-0009 on 2022-12-15 Report written: 29 Dec 2022

What happened

Field staff reported that the wellhead was cold and the pump jack was straining with a heavy, uneven load. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0015-0009 showed the wellhead at 10.5 °C with the air at 6.5 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. The downhole pump was stuck, most likely from sand or scale. Sandstone Rod & Pump's workover rig was busy on other wells, so the well waited about 8 days for it; the work itself took about 2 days.

Root cause

A worn plunger that let sand settle and lock the pump.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 0 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).

Work done

  1. Rigged up the company workover rig on the well.
  2. Pulled the rods and the insert pump.
  3. Inspected the pump: sand in the barrel and a worn plunger.
  4. Ran in a new insert pump.
  5. Re-spaced the pump and hung the rods back on.

Summary of the fix: pulled and replaced downhole pump.

Testing and return to service

Pump test confirmed fluid to surface and the wellhead warmed back to normal. The well was returned to production.

  • Review sand control on this well.
  • Send the old pump for teardown.

Maintenance Report — MNT-0015-004

Asset: WELL-0015 (SW-23 Well 015, T200, Southwest Block 23) Equipment: flowline Work started: 24 Feb 2023 08:00 · Finished: 25 Feb 2023 08:00 · Well stopped for this job: 24 hours Crew lead: Kevin Price (U-303) · Crew: Megan Ward, Daniel Foster Triggered by: inspection INS-0015-0019 on 2023-02-23 Report written: 26 Feb 2023

What happened

The weekly drone inspection INS-0015-0019 at 07:45 on 2023-02-23 found crude oil on the pad: about 7.7% of the pad area, estimated 3.9 bbl. The inspector noted: "Oil sheen around cellar." The field operator shut the well in, closed the flowline valve and placed earth berms and absorbent pads. The release was contained about 1.4 hours after the inspection. The crew traced the leak to the flanged flowline connection at the wellhead cellar.

Root cause

A failed gasket on the flange where the flowline leaves the wellhead.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 0 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).

Work done

  1. Cleaned free oil out of the cellar.
  2. Unbolted the flange and removed the failed gasket.
  3. Fitted a new gasket and new bolts, torqued to specification.
  4. Excavated the stained soil around the cellar.

Summary of the fix: replaced the flange gasket and bolts and remediated soil.

Testing and return to service

Pressure-tested the repaired section at 275 psi (1.25 × the flowline's maximum operating pressure of 220 psi) and held it for 4 hours with no pressure drop (WS-05). The well was returned to production.

Spill clean-up and waste

  • About 2.7 m³ of stained soil excavated, bagged and sent to an approved disposal site under waste manifest WM-0015-004 (WS-06).
  • 2 soil samples taken around the spill; the highest result after clean-up was 0.4% TPH, below the 1.0% target (SR-03).

The field operator shut the well in, closed the flowline valve and placed earth berms and absorbent pads. The release was contained about 3.7 hours after the inspection. The crew traced the leak to a threaded coupling on the flowline close to the wellhead.

Root cause

  • Hot work permit issued for welding; gas test before welding read 0% LEL, below the 10% limit (WS-04).

Work done

  1. Excavated around the coupling.
  2. Cut out the failed coupling and the pipe ends.
  3. Welded in new pipe and a new fitting.
  4. Coated the new joints.
  5. Excavated the stained soil.
  6. Backfilled after the pressure test.

maintenance.report_html:
Maintenance Report — MNT-0015-030

Asset: WELL-0015 (SW-23 Well 015, T200, Southwest Block 23) Equipment: pump jack Work started: 13 Mar 2026 08:00 · Finished: 21 Apr 2026 10:00 · Well stopped for this job: 938 hours Crew lead: Kevin Price (U-303) · Crew: Megan Ward Triggered by: inspection INS-0015-0175 on 2026-03-12 Report written: 22 Apr 2026

What happened

Field staff reported that oil was dripping from the gearbox onto the pump jack base. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0015-0175 showed the wellhead at 16.5 °C with the air at 11.4 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. The input shaft seal was worn and the gearbox oil level was below the sight glass. The well stayed shut in for about 37 days longer than the repair itself because heavy rain made the lease road impassable for the service truck.

Root cause

Seal wear, made worse by heat and a low oil level.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 0 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).

Work done

  1. Drained the gearbox oil into a closed container.
  2. Replaced the input and output shaft seals.
  3. Cleaned the base and absorbed the spilled oil.
  4. Refilled with the specified gear oil to the correct level.

Summary of the fix: replaced gearbox seals and topped up oil.

Testing and return to service

Ran the unit for 1 hour and checked both shafts for leaks: none found. The well was returned to production.

Waste

  • Used gear oil and oily pads sent to an approved disposal site under waste manifest WM-0015-030 (WS-06).
